title_en: Jiang Weimin v. Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd. — dispute over a house lease contract
ruling_gist_en: A lessor who provides leased property to a lessee shall comply with the purpose of the lease. A lessor engaged in the business of housing leasing shall test and treat indoor air quality to meet relevant national environmental standards. If a lessor provides leased housing with harmful gases exceeding the standards, infringing upon the lessee's life and health safety and making it impossible to achieve the purpose of the lease, and the lessee requests rescission of the contract and refund of rent and other expenses, the people's court shall support such request.

full_text_en:
Jiang Weimin v. Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd.
— Dispute over House Lease Contract

【Ruling Summary】

The lessor shall provide the leased property to the lessee in a condition suitable for the intended use. A lessor engaged in the business of leasing houses shall test and treat the indoor air quality to ensure it meets the relevant national environmental standards. Where the lessor provides a leased house with harmful gas concentrations exceeding the standards, thereby infringing on the lessee’s right to life and health and rendering the lessee’s purpose of leasing unattainable, the people’s court shall support the lessee’s claim to rescind the contract and to have the rent and other fees refunded.

Plaintiff: Jiang Weimin, male, Han ethnicity, born on July 15, 1996, residing in Duchang County, Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dongshan Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal representative: Chen Junhong, General Manager of the company.

The plaintiff, Jiang Weimin, filed an action with the Jiangning District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongyang Company), over a dispute concerning a house lease contract.

Plaintiff’s Allegations: In March 2021, the plaintiff leased from the defendant a house located at Unit X, Building X, Jiangning District, Nanjing, and the parties signed a *House Lease Contract*. The contract stipulated a monthly rent of RMB 1,100, with a deposit equal to one month’s rent and quarterly rent payment. On the date of signing, the plaintiff moved into the house in question and later began to experience physical discomfort, and his pregnant wife also fell ill. The plaintiff immediately negotiated with the defendant about exchanging the house or terminating the lease, but the defendant was unwilling to address the issue. Having no other option, the plaintiff hired a testing agency at his own expense in June of the same year to test the indoor air quality of the house. The test report showed that the levels of formaldehyde and total volatile organic compounds (TVOC) in the indoor air exceeded the standards. Considering his wife’s pregnancy, the plaintiff refused to continue living in the house, but after multiple attempts to negotiate a lease termination with the defendant, no result was achieved. To protect his own rights and interests, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit and requested a judgment: (1) rescinding the *House Lease Contract* between the plaintiff and the defendant; (2) ordering the defendant to immediately refund all fees paid by the plaintiff, totaling RMB 6,556 (details: RMB 3,300 rent paid on March 28, 2021, RMB 1,056 property management fee, RMB 1,100 deposit, and RMB 1,100 rent paid on May 16, 2021); (3) ordering the defendant to bear the litigation costs.

Defendant’s Defense: The plaintiff, Jiang Weimin, failed to pay the rent on time as agreed, thus constituting a breach of contract. After the plaintiff filed the lawsuit, the defendant independently tested the indoor harmful gases, and the results showed no exceedance of the standards. Therefore, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff’s claims.

Facts Found by the Jiangning District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province at First Instance:

The defendant, Hongyang Company, is engaged in businesses such as real estate brokerage and housing leasing. On March 21, 2021, Hongyang Company (Party A) and the plaintiff, Jiang Weimin (Party B), signed a *House Lease Contract* under which Party A leased to Party B the house located at Unit X, Building X, Jiangning District, Nanjing, for a term from March 22, 2021 to July 15, 2022; the monthly rent was RMB 1,100, with a deposit equal to one month’s rent and quarterly rent payment, the first installment of RMB 3,300 to be paid on March 22, 2021, and the second installment of RMB 3,300 to be paid on May 15 of the same year, and so on; Party A collected from Party B a security deposit of RMB 1,100, and RMB 1,056 for public area cleaning, maintenance, broadband, and property management fees. The contract also contained other terms. After signing the contract, the defendant delivered the house to the plaintiff, and the plaintiff paid RMB 3,300 in rent, RMB 1,056 in property management fees, and RMB 1,100 in deposit, totaling RMB 5,456, for which the defendant issued a receipt on March 28, 2021. On May 16, 2021, the plaintiff paid an additional rent of RMB 1,100.

In April 2021, the plaintiff’s wife (who was pregnant) experienced physical discomfort and went to hospitals such as Jiangsu Provincial People’s Hospital and General Hospital of the Eastern Theater Command for examinations, where she was diagnosed with chronic glomerulonephritis. The plaintiff believed that this was related to excessive indoor formaldehyde levels, so he purchased formaldehyde test strips and tested the air himself; the results showed excessive levels. The plaintiff then contacted the business representative of the defendant to request lease termination. During negotiations, the defendant’s staff contacted the plaintiff on June 1, 2021, to demand payment of the remaining second-installment rent. The plaintiff requested that the defendant cooperate in finding a qualified testing agency to test formaldehyde, to which the staff replied, “You rent a house and still want formaldehyde testing? If you have such conditions, you should buy a house yourself.” “In all my years, this is the first time I’ve heard of a tenant asking for formaldehyde testing.” “Live if you want; if not, move out tonight—I can find tenants who don’t care about formaldehyde or acetaldehyde.” After negotiations with the defendant failed, the plaintiff hired Jiangsu Zhiran Testing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhiran Company) to test the air quality of the house in question. On June 2, 2021, Zhiran Company conducted on-site sampling. On June 7, 2021, Zhiran Company issued a test report [No. (2021) Su Zhi Jian (Shi Huan) Zi No. (202106090)], showing the following results: formaldehyde test value 0.213 mg/m³, benzene test value 0.035 mg/m³, toluene test value 0.062 mg/m³, xylene test value 0.085 mg/m³, TVOC test value 0.863 mg/m³; formaldehyde and TVOC failed to meet the standards. After obtaining the test report, the plaintiff moved out of the leased house, notified the defendant, and returned the keys to the house by mail.

After further investigation, it was found that according to the *Indoor Air Quality Standard* (GB/T18883-2002) jointly issued by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine, the Ministry of Health, and the State Environmental Protection Administration, the indoor formaldehyde concentration shall be less than or equal to 0.10 mg/m³, and the TVOC concentration shall be less than or equal to 0.60 mg/m³. Zhiran Company holds a China Metrology Accreditation (CMA) certificate (No. 171012050167) and has the appropriate qualifications for environmental and environmental protection testing.

It was also found that on June 29, 2021, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court regarding this dispute. The court arranged pre-litigation mediation through a specially invited mediation organization, and the copy of the complaint and the evidence materials were served on the defendant by the mediation organization on July 3, 2021.

During the trial, the defendant stated that the house in question had been decorated in 2017, and although no testing was conducted upon completion of the decoration, the defendant tested the indoor air quality after the plaintiff filed the lawsuit, and the results were compliant. The defendant submitted a test report issued by Zhiran Company [No. (2021) Su Zhi Jian (Shi Huan) Zi No. (202111452)], with sampling conducted on November 18, 2021, showing a formaldehyde test value of 0.090 mg/m³ and a TVOC test value of 0.424 mg/m³, both within the national standards. On November 26, 2021, the court went to Zhiran Company to investigate the inconsistency between the two test reports. The legal representative of Zhiran Company stated that the instruments, testing methods, and standards used for the two tests were the same, but the volatilization rates of formaldehyde and TVOC are heavily influenced by environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and sealing time. The two reports were nearly six months apart, and harmful substances may decrease over time as they volatilize. Based on the numerical values in the reports, even in winter (when volatility decreases with temperature), the formaldehyde value was close to the upper limit of the national standard.

Opinion of the Jiangning District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province at First Instance:

The core obligation of the lessor is to provide the lessee with a leased property that is fit for the intended use and has the value of use and profitability. Where the lessor provides a leased house with harmful gas levels exceeding the standards, this infringes on the lessee’s personality rights centering on safety and health, thereby rendering the lessee’s purpose of leasing unattainable. Therefore, such a house should not be leased out, and the lessor of a house already leased is not entitled to collect rent. The lessee has the right to request rescission of the contract and a refund of all payments.

In this case, the defendant, Hongyang Company, as an enterprise engaged in the business of house leasing, should proactively test and treat the indoor air quality to ensure it meets the relevant national environmental standards. Where the defendant neither proactively tested the indoor air quality nor cooperated with the lessee in conducting such testing, the plaintiff, Jiang Weimin, is entitled to hire a qualified testing agency to perform the test on his own, and the defendant may not refuse to acknowledge the test results on the ground that the test was unilaterally conducted by the plaintiff. According to the test report submitted by the plaintiff, the levels of formaldehyde and TVOC in the house leased by the defendant were seriously above the standards, potentially causing severe health damage to the occupants. Although there is no conclusive evidence to prove that the plaintiff’s wife’s illness was caused by these harmful gases, the possibility cannot be ruled out that it was related to factors such as reduced immunity due to excessive harmful gases. Although the defendant also submitted a test report from the same testing agency showing that the indoor air quality was compliant, the test was conducted a considerable time after the plaintiff moved in. Given the volatile nature of the gases, the test values for the relevant harmful gases may decrease over time, temperature, ventilation, or treatment, and therefore this report cannot prove that the air quality was compliant during the plaintiff’s occupancy. Furthermore, based on the values in the second report, even in winter (when harmful gas volatility is weaker) and nearly half a year later, the formaldehyde value was close to the upper limit of the national standard, which further corroborates the correctness of the first report.

In summary, the *House Lease Contract* in this case should be rescinded. The plaintiff’s claim for rescission reached the defendant on July 3, 2021, when the copy of the complaint was served on Hongyang Company through the court’s specially invited mediation organization; therefore, the house lease contract was rescinded on that date. After the contract is rescinded, the defendant shall refund all payments made by the plaintiff, totaling RMB 6,556.

Accordingly, in accordance with Articles 3, paragraph 1(4) of Article 563, paragraph 2 of Article 565, paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 566, and Article 708 of the *Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China*, and paragraph 1 of Article 64 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China*, the Jiangning District People’s Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on December 7, 2021:

1. The *House Lease Contract* between the plaintiff, Jiang Weimin, and the defendant, Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd., is rescinded as of July 3, 2021;

2. The defendant, Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd., shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, refund to the plaintiff, Jiang Weimin, RMB 4,400 in rent, RMB 1,056 in property management fees, and RMB 1,100 in deposit, totaling RMB 6,556.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 294, reduced by half to RMB 147, shall be borne by the defendant, Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd.

Hongyang Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal with the Nanjing Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province. Because Hongyang Company, having been lawfully served with summons, failed to appear in court without justifiable reason, the Nanjing Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province ruled on February 17, 2022, as follows:

This case is treated as a withdrawal of the appeal by the appellant, Nanjing Hongyang Real Estate Agency Co., Ltd. The first-instance judgment shall become legally effective from the date this ruling is served.

This ruling is final.
